_comment: A mythological reminder + a moral, spoken by the narrator after each boss falls (moral_<realm> for the final boss, moral_mini_<realm> for the palier). Queued after the boss-fall lines. Modal.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The Hydra grew two heads for each one cut — so the Greeks taught that some evils only multiply when met with brute force alone.
The lesson of Lerna: strike the root, not the symptom. Wisdom ends what the sword cannot.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Rangda and the lion Barong wrestle forever, and neither truly wins — for Bali, good and evil are not foes to destroy but forces to keep in balance.
Remember: to crave only victory is to misread the dance of the world.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Each night Apophis swallowed the sun, and each dawn it rose again — Egypt's promise that chaos is never the final word.
Light returns to those who endure the dark. Hold to that when your own night runs long.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The gods bound Fenrir only by sacrifice — Tyr laid his hand in the wolf's jaws knowing he would lose it, to keep a promise.
The Norse honoured the price of an oath kept. Ask yourself what your word is worth.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Susanoo felled Orochi not by force but by guile, drowning its eight heads in sake — Japan's reminder that cunning unmakes what raw power cannot.
The patient and the clever outlast the proud.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: From the torn body of Cipactli the gods shaped the world — the Aztecs knew creation is always paid for in destruction.
Every harvest feeds on what came before. Take nothing as freely given; all is owed.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The Cyclops Polyphemus was undone by Odysseus's wit, not his blade — Greece warned that strength without sight is easily blinded.
Brawn with no cunning makes only a larger fool.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The bhuta are spirits of the unburied and unmourned — Bali teaches that the dead we neglect become the dead enraged.
Honour what you leave behind, lest it follow you down.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The Sphinx devoured all who failed her riddle, until one man simply dared to answer — Egypt's lesson that the deadliest gate yields to a clear mind.
Fear the question less than the refusal to think.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Trolls turn to stone at the first touch of dawn — the Norse knew that what thrives in darkness cannot bear the light of day.
Drag your fears into the sun, and watch them harden and crack.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The tengu punish the boastful and the proud who wear piety as a mask — Japan's warning against arrogance dressed as virtue.
Humility is the only wing on which one truly rises.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The jaguar knights were the bravest of warriors — yet even they were given to feed the hungry sun.
Mictlan reminds you: courage is no exemption from the end. Every hunter is, in time, the hunted.
